overview: Circular financing deepens as chipmakers invest in AI startups
Multimodal decision APIs aim to cut costs and latency
Cell‑level genomics models boost disease‑variant research

top.title: Taiwan’s chipmaking giant TSMC to invest $1B in Anthropic, OpenAI
top.summary: TSMC will invest $1 billion—$500 m in OpenAI preferred stock and $500 m in Anthropic shares—linking its chip production to AI developers amid record profits and concerns over circular financing.

top.title: Gemini Decisions API: Fast, calibrated multimodal decisions
top.summary: Google launches Gemini Decisions API, using Gemini Decision 1 to score up to 1,000 multimodal yes/no or multiple‑choice queries in a single pass, offering sub‑second latency and lower cost per token.

top.title: AlphaGenome 2: Deciphering how cells read DNA to better understand disease
top.summary: DeepMind releases AlphaGenome 2, a conditional model predicting DNA variant effects for specific cell types and states, trained on 100 M single‑cell profiles, doubling variant detection versus its predecessor.

top.title: Google’s AlphaGenome 2 zooms in on the cellular roots of disease
top.summary: The Verge reports AlphaGenome 2 provides finer‑grained predictions of genetic variant impacts across cell types, aiding disease research and drug targeting by turning static cell atlases into a predictive genetics engine.

top.title: JioStar’s chief architect on AI discovery at 500M-user scale
top.summary: JioStar’s chief architect Vijay Seshadri shares lessons on scaling AI evaluation, guardrails, and production deployment for a user base of 500 million.

top.title: PSI is trying to make a business out of AI-driven scientific discovery
top.summary: Startup PSI uses Anthropic’s Fable 5.2 to solve the Aaronson‑Ambainis conjecture, showcasing AI‑driven scientific discovery and aiming to commercialize breakthroughs in quantum computing and other physics domains.
